_comment: EXAMPLE manifest, trimmed to three fictionalized entries for the public showcase.
Manifest of Slack channel canvases and the skills each one describes.
Single source for: the coverage table in README.md, the publish script, and the
canvas-drift check in .github/workflows/canvas-drift.yml. Add a row here when a
skill starts delivering into a new channel, and record canvas_id once published.
Every canvas with a canvas_id here is published. To change one, edit its source file
and call canvases.edit with the canvas_id below and a document_content replace
operation. conversations.canvases.create again makes a SECOND canvas.
The TITLE cannot be changed after creation: canvases.edit rejects a title
argument, so a retitle means delete + recreate. Always pass title on create.

canvases.title: Applied AI Channel Agent Description
canvases.notes: Several jobs in one channel: primer notices, the thread-hygiene digest, the Monday pipeline brief, and the suggestion inbox plus every operational notice that used to be a DM. The skills listed after weekly-pipeline-brief are here only for their routed suggestions and notices — their own reports are documented on their own channels.

canvases.title: Repo Health Agent Description
canvases.notes: Published via conversations.canvases.create (channel canvas, not standalone). Verified before create that conversations.info reported properties.canvas null, so this is the only canvas on the channel. To change it, edit repo-health.md then canvases.edit with this canvas_id and a document_content replace; a second create makes a duplicate. @bot is a member, so create did not fail not_in_channel. Channel exists to keep the repo audit out of #applied-ai, which is a delivery channel this skill also reports on; the product_or_architecture items it routes under _shared/thread-feedback.md still go to #applied-ai, which is why that skill appears on both entries.

no_canvas.reason: Building block. No Slack delivery of its own.
Building block. No Slack delivery of its own; described inside the market-intel-analysis canvas, which is the skill that calls it.
